title: What is the difference between Event Notification (a minimal event carrying just an id + event name + a link to fetch details) and Event-Carried State Transfer (the event carries the data consumers need), what is the "fat event / god event" anti-pattern (broadcasting the whole aggregate "just in case"), and how do you decide between the two (coupling vs extra calls, with versioned schemas either way)?
shortTitle: Event Notification versus Event-Carried State Transfer
keyPoints: Event Notification sends a tiny pointer (event ID, aggregate ID, link) and makes consumers call back for details.
Event-Carried State Transfer includes the data consumers need so they act without calling back.
The fat event / god event anti-pattern broadcasts the entire aggregate state just in case, leaking internals and bloating the topic.
Event Notification couples consumers to the producer at runtime; State Transfer couples them to the schema at design time.
Favor State Transfer when consumer autonomy matters, callback load is heavy, or consumers maintain local read models.
Favor Notification when data is large/sensitive or freshness is critical so a stale snapshot is unacceptable.
Both styles need a versioned schema (Avro/Protobuf + Schema Registry) because both create consumer-facing contracts.

s1_definition.oneliner: Event Notification sends a tiny pointer and makes consumers call back; Event-Carried State Transfer sends the data consumers need so they act independently; never send the whole aggregate just in case.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Event Notification** – the event carries minimal data (event ID, event type, aggregate ID, timestamp, and usually a link), and the consumer must call back to the producer to fetch the details it needs.
- **Event-Carried State Transfer** – the event includes the data consumers need directly, so consumers act without any callback to the producer.
- **Fat event / god event** – the anti-pattern of serializing the entire aggregate and broadcasting it just in case some consumer might want something, which leaks internals and bloats the topic.
- **Trade-off** – Event Notification gives smaller payloads and always-fresh data but adds runtime coupling; State Transfer gives consumer autonomy and resilience at the cost of larger payloads and snapshot staleness.
- **Versioned schema** – both styles create a contract that consumers depend on, so both must use a versioned schema like Avro or Protobuf.
s1_definition.analogy: When a transfer completes at National Bank of India, the transfer department can tell the SMS department in two ways. Event Notification is a short memo: "Transfer T-123 happened for account SAV2001 - call us if you need details." The SMS department phones back to get the amount and beneficiary. Event-Carried State Transfer is a fuller memo: "Transfer T-123: Rs.50000 to BENEF-77 from SAV2001" - now the SMS department acts immediately without phoning back. The fat-event anti-pattern is photocopying the department's entire internal file, every private note, risk score, and scratch calculation, and mailing it to everyone just in case.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Event Notification
  ──────────────────
  Transfer Svc         Kafka          Notification Svc
      │                  │                  │
      │── tiny event ───▶│                  │
      │  {id, type, link}│                  │
      │                  │── deliver ──────▶│
      │                  │                  │── callback: GET /transfers/TXN-123
      │◀────────────────────────────────────│
      │── details ─────────────────────────▶│
      │                  │                  │── send SMS
      │                  │                  │
  Producer must be UP for callback


  Event-Carried State Transfer
  ────────────────────────────
  Transfer Svc         Kafka          Notification Svc
      │                  │                  │
      │── rich event ───▶│                  │
      │  {id, from, to,  │                  │
      │   amount, currency}                 │
      │                  │── deliver ──────▶│
      │                  │                  │── send SMS (no callback!)
      │                  │                  │
  Producer can be DOWN, consumer still works


  Fat Event (Anti-Pattern)
  ────────────────────────
  Transfer Svc         Kafka          All Consumers
      │                  │                  │
      │── EVERYTHING ───▶│                  │
      │  {id, from, to,  │                  │
      │   amount, fee,   │── deliver ──────▶│
      │   ledgerRef,     │                  │
      │   riskBucket,    │  Consumers see   │
      │   balance,       │  internal fields │
      │   auditNotes...} │  they should not │
      │                  │                  │
  Leaks internals, bloats topic, couples everyone
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Event Notification and Event-Carried State Transfer are two ways to shape an event, and the difference is what the consumer has to do next. Event Notification keeps the event tiny, just an event ID, aggregate ID, and a link, and the consumer calls back to the producer for details. The upside is small payloads and always-fresh data; the downside is runtime coupling because the consumer depends on the producer being up for the callback. Event-Carried State Transfer puts the data consumers need inside the event, so the consumer acts with no callback at all. The upside is autonomy and resilience; the downside is larger payloads and a snapshot that may be slightly stale by consumption time.

The fat event or god event is what happens when you over-apply State Transfer and dump the entire aggregate into the event just in case. At National Bank of India, an early version of the transfer event included the internal ledger reference, risk bucket, and sender's balance. When the team renamed `riskBucket` internally, it broke the fraud scoring consumer because that team had started depending on the field. The fix was to design the event around the meaningful domain fact, including only the fields consumers legitimately need, and treat the schema as a curated contract.

In practice, Event-Carried State Transfer with curated fields is the better default for event-driven systems, because it gives consumer autonomy, resilience, and the ability to maintain local read models. Use Event Notification only when the data is too large or sensitive to carry, or when freshness is so critical that a stale snapshot is unacceptable. A pragmatic hybrid carries the commonly needed fields and includes a link for the rare consumer that needs the full current state.

Remember one sentence: carry the data consumers need in the event so they act autonomously, but curate the fields deliberately and never broadcast the whole aggregate as a god event.
